note: Which drawn pipe belongs to which vacuum volume, and which valve joins which two volumes. Read from the names queezz gave the pipes in diagram.svg, never from where the lines happen to sit on the page. The vacuum state derived from this is a prediction from the valve positions an operator has entered, not a pressure measurement.

drawing.note: The field the drawing is painted on, how much wider the reading aid draws a coloured pipe, and the inks that are not vacuum states. `pump_stopped_edge` is the dark grey a stopped pump's rim and inner lines wear so the whole pump recedes (queezz, 2026-09-08, letter 20260908-e2498698-5c9c50: 'we can also gray out pump edges and lines. Dark gray. So it speaks more loudly that that is closed'); a running pump keeps the black he drew. `sealed_stripe` and `sealed_period` are the hatch a sealed volume's own vessel body wears over its remembered colour, and `sealed_pale` is how far the same volume's pipes, tees, crosses, gauge stems and open valves are moved toward the ground instead -- because a hatch painted onto a 4 px stroke is a dashed line, and queezz read dashed pipes as broken ones three letters running on 2026-09-09 (`20260908-b1c0ba9c-342679`, `20260908-a8f73fdc-616055`, `20260908-db3ff048-8394c2`): 'I don't like the broken lines. They are pipes. That reads like a breakage', and 'the dashed valve, it's like guess what shape this is and what this blob does'. So the hatch is on the two chamber bodies alone, every pipe is solid in every state, and a valve is never hatched at all. The paler tone sits below the palette's own 3:1 floor against the field on purpose: a sealed pipe is not a live claim. See `sealed_state` below. The field is a quiet warm stone so the state colours are the loudest thing on the page (owner permission 2026-09-08). `band` is the widening the More switch offers; `band_default` is false since 0.15.0, because queezz's own strokes are the width he wants (letter 20260908-c8ef7df5-5f5e40) and a widening he did not ask for is the app talking over his drawing. `valve_closed` and `valve_closed_edge` are the two inks a shut valve wears: white with a black outline, the one dark-rimmed shape on the drawing, so it stands out as the break (queezz, 2026-09-08, letter 20260908-3308e02d-3021dd: 'When closed, black border white fill is good. Stands out'). An open valve wears the colour flowing through it as fill *and* outline — 'I think I like the valves edge to be same color as the fill' — so it reads as part of the pipe at every valve size, gas panel included. `flange` is the blank-flange tone: a light steel that is neither the open green nor the closed grey nor any state colour, worn by the probe segment when a blank is installed in place of the probe. A stopped pump has no ink here at all, on purpose: it keeps the grey queezz drew it in, because that grey already means off. 0.16.0 made a stopped pump yellow, on a relayed line that said 'stays as drawn (yellow)' — the drawing's own fill is grey, and the yellow was the app's own *on* colour. His answer, immediately (letter 20260908-93fb84a6-5a69cf): 'No, no! Blue and yellow, yellow reads like on. Gray for off was lost. Why? WHY???' So yellow appears nowhere on a pump any more, the operator palette no longer paints one either, and the prediction writes a fill only for a pump that is running.

states_note: Six roles. They were redrawn on 2026-09-08 as seven, twice in one day, and the seventh was retired the same evening (see the end of this note). queezz on the first seven: 'Gas color and rough vacuum color are indistinguishable', and, amending the brief that produced them, 'I don't want muted, actually. No color blind people here. But those colors are nicer than maxed RGBs. So design nice, not color blind nice. Tol inspired is still fine' (letters 20260908-92656592-3a679a and 20260908-630efd50-e4c7ab). So the ladder-of-weight rule that made them all crowd the dark end is gone: the five coloured ones and the grey now sit at nearly one lightness (L* 42 to 52) and are told apart by **hue**, which is what a 4 px line and a legend chip actually carry. Every one still clears 3:1 both on the stone field and against the gas panel's green valve, which caps a colour's own luminance at about 0.204 — that cap is the floor's price, and it is why these are deep jewel tones rather than Tol's own lightness. Chroma is spent rather than saved: C* 54 to 76 for the six, against 35 to 55 before. The pairs are checked by arithmetic, not by eye: every pair is at least 21 CIEDE2000 units apart (the closest of the seven was the plasma blue against the sealed teal, 21.3, where the old palette's closest was 11.6; with the teal gone the closest pair is wider still), and gas and rough vacuum now sit in different hue families — magenta at 332 degrees against amber at 73 — where before they were plum and ochre, both warm and both dark. High vacuum stays split in two ('I think I'd rather have two high vacuum colors. Upstream and downstream. To see mixing clearly'), and a high-vacuum volume takes its colour from the vessel it is joined to. `isolated` is the one deliberately grey of the six and stays the quietest on the field: it is the absence of a claim, not a seventh thing competing for the eye. **The teal seventh, `sealed`, was retired on 2026-09-08** by the owner's own correction (letters 20260908-fe94c769-493d71 and 20260908-2c3d9837-37ab4a): 'between the turbo and its gate, the vacuum is High, not pumped sealed off. Not sealed. Pumped sealed off means I pump, close the valve. Vacuum holds, and degrades per the vessel's leak rate.' A volume with a running pump on it now wears that pump's own state — the stub behind a closed gate is high vacuum in the turbo's side colour — and *sealed off* stopped being a colour of its own and became a **remembered** state, described in `sealed_state`.

states.label: Gas
states.meaning: a bottle or N2 is open, and its symbol is drawn in the vessel

states.label: High vacuum, plasma side
states.meaning: a turbo reaches it, and so does the plasma vessel

states.label: High vacuum, QMS side
states.meaning: a turbo reaches it, and so does the QMS vessel

states.label: Isolated, unknown
states.meaning: nothing open to it, and no record of what it last held

sealed_state.note: Sealed off is not a colour of its own; it is one of the six above, remembered, with a date on it. queezz, 2026-09-08 (letter 20260908-2c3d9837-37ab4a): 'Sealed off with good vacuum 3 days ago says something... If we have air/N2 or isolation especially in the main two vessels, we need to keep a date so we can say: ah, that upstream was under N2 for two weeks!' So an isolated volume that has a memory wears the colour of what it was LAST under, hatched, and the readout says what and for how long; `isolated` grey is left for a volume with no memory at all. The hatch was chosen over the lighter treatment the same letter offered because a lighter treatment cannot hold the palette's own 3:1 floor against the stone field: lightening the six by even 20 per cent toward white drops the QMS green to 2.42 and rough vacuum to 2.38, measured. A hatch keeps every coloured pixel at full strength and marks the volume by texture instead, and it is one mechanism for both a filled body and a drawn line.
sealed_state.label: Sealed off, holding
sealed_state.meaning: closed and holding whatever it was last under; the readout says what, and since when

memory_note: What the prediction remembers per volume so it can say 'sealed, was high vacuum, 1 day': the last state it was in while something reached it, the moment it became isolated, and the gas symbols it held if that state was gas. It lives under `_volumes` in `elements_state.json`, beside the valve positions, so it survives a restart; it is rebuilt by replaying `logs.csv` when the state file has none, so a fresh machine still knows; and it is a plain argument to `predict()`, so the practice mode can run the same predictor over its own copy without touching the recorded one.
hint_thresholds_note: The thresholds the readout's advice changes at, written down because queezz asked for them to be said out loud. `bake_air_days` is shorter than `bake_gas_days` on purpose: air brings water vapour in and dry nitrogen does not. `fresh_vacuum_days` is how long a vacuum stays fresh enough that opening the turbo straight in may be fine rather than roughing through the bypass first.
volumes_note: A `vessel` is the drawn body of a chamber and a `junction` a small one (a tee, a cross); both say their state by their body rather than by an outline. A vessel also declares, since 0.15.0, the `high_vacuum` colour anything joined to it wears, its `rank` (the lower one leads when the two chambers are joined, which puts the plasma vessel first), and a `symbol_box` -- the rectangle inside its drawn shape where a gas symbol may stand. The box is written here rather than derived because the plasma vessel is a cross, not a rectangle, and the middle of its bounding box is not the middle of anything a circle fits in; a test proves each box really is inside the shape it names, so an edit in Inkscape that moved a vessel cannot leave a symbol floating outside it.

probe-line.note: Four drawn segments meeting at one cross, and one volume. queezz split the run in Inkscape on 2026-09-08 (letter 20260908-520505af-9047d4) so a blank flange could be shown: `probe-pipe` now stops at the cross instead of running through it, and `probe-pipe-cross-to-GVBD` carries on from the cross down to GVBD. The cross itself joins all four — the probe segment from above, the line from bypass-l1 across, and the GVBD segment below — so they are one continuous space and there is no valve between them to split them at. What the split buys is a *segment the drawing can paint on its own*: under the Blank configuration the probe segment wears the blank-flange tone while the rest of this volume keeps its predicted colour. Adding `probe-pipe-cross-to-GVBD` here is also the repair of a real gap: it was drawn but unmapped, so nothing coloured it at all.
probe-line.label: Probe line

gas-manifold.label: Gas manifold to the plasma vessel

pumps_note: `serves` is the vessel a turbo belongs to, and it is a fact about the rig rather than about today's valve positions: TMPU is the plasma vessel's turbo whether or not GVU is open. A running pump wears what it is doing — a turbo the high-vacuum colour of the side it serves, a rotary or a scroll the rough-vacuum colour — and a stopped one is left exactly as drawn, in his own grey (queezz, 2026-09-08, letters 20260908-3688eabd-587dfe, 'why don't we change the TMP on color to its HV color? Same for rough pumps', and 20260908-93fb84a6-5a69cf, 'Gray for off was lost. Why? WHY???'). Every pump here already had an on/off an operator presses and confirms, recorded in history like a valve, and the prediction has always read it: a stopped turbo makes no high vacuum, and never did. **`stopped: "passage"` is a turbo's second state** (owner ruling 2026-09-09, letter 20260908-948b8dbc-b1eb0d): queezz, watching TMPD stopped with the QMS rotary running on its backing line, 'The rough pump pumps, it can really do that.' Gas goes through a stationary rotor, so a turbo that is not running is a piece of pipe: it joins its own `volume` (its inlet line) to its `backed_by` line exactly as an open valve would, and the vessel above a stopped TMPD with GVD open is rough vacuum, pumped by the QMS rotary through the stopped turbo. A running turbo is the pump again and the wall again. Only a closed valve blocks. A rough pump carries neither field: it exhausts to the room, so it joins nothing when it stops.
gas_sources_note: `symbol` is what the bottle wears on the drawing, and since 0.15.0 it is also drawn large inside any vessel the gas reaches (queezz, 2026-09-08: 'we can put a gas in a circle (same as the bottle sign) inside the plasma vessel. Ar, O2, H2. So it's visible big at a glance'). Several gases open at once draw several circles. Nothing is derived from the gas name: the symbol is written here beside it.

line_configuration.note: What sits in the narrow pipe between the two vessels, from the Line configuration annotation an operator sets on the Vacuum page. Only 'Pipe open' is a connection: with a membrane installed, something is mounted across the whole pipe and each valve on it opens onto its own private side of the barrier, so the two vessels are separate spaces (owner review 2026-09-08). Boron deposition uses the same pipe, but its far (downstream) end is not joined at all: queezz, 2026-09-08 (letter 20260907-dc825e44-e6d89e) -- 'Boron uses same pipe. But other end not connected to downstream. Could be pumped from plasma side via bypass.' -- so `dead_end_valve` names the downstream valve that never reaches this pipe in that mode, whatever position it is in; the pipe then simply takes the plasma side's own predicted state (or isolated, if even that side is shut), and it can still be pumped from the plasma side through the bypass manifold because that reach never ran through this pipe's far end. Until an operator has recorded which configuration applies, the prediction does not claim a connection nobody has told it about. `linked_valve` names the drawn valve this whole annotation also governs directly (owner decision 2026-09-08, same letter: 'Membrane installed and the membrane valve should be linked') -- it has no press of its own any more, closed only under `closed_mode` and open under every other configuration, so its own colour and what it does to the diagram's connectivity can never disagree.
line_configuration.four_note: The four queezz actually runs, in his own order and his own words (owner decision 2026-09-08, letter 20260908-b429ce4b-2ad897): '1. membrane installed. 2. pipe open, but the membrane probe in or bellows, which is vacuum wise the same. 3. blank, bellows not connected. 4. boron deposition sample holder installed. Are good and actual variants we run now.' `order` is that order and the card follows it; `meaning` is the one line the card's More prints beside each. **Blank** is vacuum-wise the same as Membrane installed — the crossover is closed at the flange — so it appears in `closed_modes` beside `membrane` and connects nothing; what it looks like is different, and that is what `flange_element` is for: the probe segment is drawn in the blank-flange tone and no plug is drawn at the membrane position, because there is no probe there to draw. `aliases` resolves any older spelling of a stored value on read, so a configuration recorded before this release still names the same mode; anything unrecognised falls back to `unknown` rather than to a guess.

membrane.label: Membrane installed
membrane.meaning: the membrane separates the two vessels at the crossover

open.label: Pipe open
open.meaning: the membrane probe is in, or the bellows — either way a vacuum connection between the vessels

blank.label: Blank
blank.meaning: the bellows is not connected and a blank flange closes the crossover; vacuum-wise like a membrane

boron.label: Boron deposition
boron.meaning: the sample holder is installed; the pipe is a plasma-side dead end, never joined to the QMS vessel

unknown.label: Not recorded
unknown.meaning: nobody has said what is mounted, so nothing is claimed

gauges_note: `stem` is the short line from a gauge symbol to the pipe or vessel it reads. queezz drew each one as an Inkscape-named path beside its gauge and asked whether the app could work with that rather than name six more elements (2026-09-08). It can: three sit inside their gauge's own group as its only plain line, and three are the plain line drawn immediately before their gauge at the top level of the drawing. Nothing was guessed — each id below is that one line, and a test proves it is still the gauge's own neighbour so a regroup in Inkscape cannot silently point a stem at the wrong volume. `kind: "ionization"` marks the two gauges that must not see gas or air while they are switched on, and it is on exactly the two whose own names say so; queezz settled the rest on 2026-09-04 — when venting, 'only ionization gauges go off (Baratron, Pirani, the Pfeiffer single gauge and the Ulvac membrane gauge work at one atmosphere)'. Nothing else here is read as an ionization gauge, and a gauge with no `kind` is simply never warned about. **Moved 2026-09-08** (owner, letter 20260908-c8ef7df5-5f5e40: 'moved the upstream IG to gauges manifold, where it is physically now for some time already'): `bypass-ionization-gauge` reads the **plasma vessel** now, not the bypass manifold — queezz moved its whole group onto the plasma vessel's gauge manifold in the drawing, beside the single gauge and the upstream Baratron, and the map follows the drawing. Its id and its stem are unchanged, because an id is his to rename and this was a move, not a rename. The bypass manifold is therefore left with one gauge and no ionization gauge at all: `bypass-absolute-gauge`, the Ulvac the two pump-down guides already send you to read.
warnings_note: The two press warnings of 0.13.0 are read from this map and from nothing else: a switched-on gauge marked `kind: "ionization"` whose volume the press would join to gas or vent air, and a running pump of `kind: "turbo"` whose own volume the press would join to vent air. A turbo is a boundary in the prediction, so the volume that matters for it is its own, never everything behind it. Both are predictions from the valve positions an operator entered — the same walk that colours the pipes — and never an interlock: nothing here reads a pressure, refuses a press, or protects any hardware.
